title: Unit – 2 : Session – 3 : SLO – 2 | Multiple Bus Structures & Expansion Bus Types
sections: Section A – Match the Following (Answers)
1. ISA → D. Industry Standard Architecture
2. Multiple Bus Architecture → A. Uses interleaved memory banks to improve performance
3. PCI → C. Peripheral Component Interconnect
4. AGP → B. Handles video-specific data transfers
5. PCMCIA → E. PC memory card interface
Section B – Fill in the Blanks
A MULTIPLE BUS is used to overcome the bandwidth limitations of a single bus system.
In a multiple bus system, memory is divided into multiple BANKS (modules) to allow parallel access.
To handle simultaneous memory requests, a BUS ARBITRATION policy is needed.
The AGP bus is specifically designed to accelerate graphics rendering.
EISA serves as an extended version of the ISA expansion bus.
Section C – Activity Task

Task 1 (described): Processors P1…PN, each with a private cache, connect to multiple buses B1…BB; the buses connect to interleaved memory banks M1…MM; hardware arbiters at each bus resolve contention.

Task 2a – Interleaved memory: consecutive addresses are spread across different banks, so while one bank is being accessed another can start a new access; overlapping accesses raise effective memory bandwidth.
Task 2b – More processors than buses: contention grows; some processors must wait for a free bus, so throughput saturates at the number of buses and arbitration delays increase.

Task 2c – Hardware arbiters: several processors may request the same bus in the same cycle; arbiters grant access according to priority/fairness rules so that transfers do not collide and every requester is eventually served.
Section D – True or False
In a multiple bus system, a processor is connected to only one bus. — FALSE
Interleaved memory allows simultaneous access to different memory banks. — TRUE
Bus allocation in a multiple bus system is handled by software scheduling. — FALSE (hardware arbiters)
The PCI bus is an expansion bus used for connecting external hardware. — TRUE
Even if some paths fail in a multiple bus architecture, the system can still operate. — TRUE
